key_insight: Randomized controlled trials are still the gold standard for measuring AI-driven human uplift, but frontier AI systems violate key RCT assumptions; the paper identifies tailored design and analysis adjustments that restore validity for high‑stakes decisions.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between classical RCT methodology and the distinctive properties of frontier AI (nonstationarity, model updates, personalization, spillovers, and emergent behaviors) that can bias human uplift estimates and mislead deployment or governance choices.
method: Systematic threat analysis: enumerate how frontier-AI features (updates, adaptivity, distribution shift, heterogenous effects, spillovers) undermine RCT assumptions and which biases result.

Practical protocol adjustments: propose design fixes (stratified/block randomization, buffer periods, spillover controls, holdout arms), analysis best practices (pre-registration, simulation-based power, sequential monitoring, heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses), and adversarial/synthetic complements.

Operational recommendations: combine RCTs with observational and synthetic-control methods, safety-focused audits, transparent reporting, and decision rules for when RCT evidence suffices for deployment governance.
impact: Provides AI/ML teams and policymakers concrete, scalable practices to produce reliable human uplift estimates from frontier systems, reducing the risk of harmful or premature deployments and informing safer governance decisions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: RCT lifecycle augmented with AI-specific checks (pre-deployment simulation, buffer periods, update freeze, adversarial tests).
Threat map: icons linking frontier-AI properties (updates, personalization, spillovers) to specific RCT failure modes and mitigation steps.
Decision flowchart: when to run an RCT vs. hybrid/synthetic approaches, including sample-size and monitoring triggers.
Before/after chart: example treatment-effect estimate shifts under naive RCT vs. corrected protocol (showing bias reduction).
paper_title: RCTs & Human Uplift Studies: Methodological Challenges and Practical Solutions for Frontier AI Evaluation
paper_authors: Patricia Paskov, Kevin Wei, Shen Zhou Hong, Dan Bateyko, Xavier Roberts-Gaal
